name: DRV8860PWPR
title: 38 V serial-controlled driver, eight low-side outputs
summary: DRV8860 and DRV8860A are eight protected low-side NMOS switches with catch diodes to VM, run from one 8 V to 38 V supply and controlled over a clocked serial link that can be daisy-chained. Each output can hold full on for a set time and then drop to a programmed PWM duty to hold a relay, solenoid or unipolar stepper coil with less heat. Overcurrent, overtemperature and undervoltage shut the outputs down; the DRV8860 also flags an open load, the DRV8860A does not. Faults are read per channel over the serial link and signalled on an open-drain nFAULT pin.
key_figures: 8 low-side NMOS, catch diodes to VM
200 mA each PW, 330 mA each PWP
1.5 Ω typ at 25 °C, 1.8 Ω typ at 85 °C (VM = 24 V, 150 mA)

notes: DRV8860A comes in PW only and has no open-load detection; DRV8860 comes in PW and PWP.

circuits.title: Typical application, eight inductive loads
circuits.description: A DRV8860PWP sinks eight coil loads, each a resistance in series with an inductance: the resistance end of every load goes to VM, the coil end to its OUT pin. VM is decoupled at the pin by 0.1 µF ceramic and 10 µF bulk. The host drives DIN, CLK, LATCH and ENABLE and reads DOUT; nFAULT is pulled to a 3.3 V rail through 4.7 kΩ and read by the host. GND and the thermal pad go to ground. Design targets: VM 8 V to 38 V, 330 mA per channel.

circuits.title: Single device on a host processor
circuits.description: Five host GPIO lines connect to LATCH, CLK, DIN, DOUT and nFAULT; nFAULT carries a pull-up resistor. Coils run from the 8 V to 38 V supply to the outputs; OUT1 and OUT8 are drawn, with OUT2 to OUT7 loaded the same way between them.
notes: VM, GND and ENABLE are outside this connection.

circuits.title: Two devices in a daisy chain
circuits.description: One host serial port drives two devices. LATCH and CLK go to both; host data enters DIN of device 1, DOUT of device 1 feeds DIN of device 2, and DOUT of device 2 returns to the host, so one 16-bit shift reaches both. Each device sinks its own coils from the 8 V to 38 V supply; OUT1 and OUT8 are drawn on each.
notes: nFAULT lines of chained devices are tied together; VM, GND and ENABLE are outside this connection.

operation.text: A logic LDO and gate drive run from VM. An 8-bit shift register fed by DIN and CLK loads one of three registers on LATCH: the 8-bit data register (output on/off), the 8-bit control register (energizing time and PWM duty) and the 16-bit fault register. Each of the eight outputs has its own gate drive, overcurrent sensing and, on the DRV8860, open-load sensing, and a diode from the output up to VM.

Usable current depends on ambient temperature, case temperature and the overall duty cycle. Eight channels on continuously: 200 mA each in PW, 330 mA each in PWP; one channel alone: 560 mA. Lower PWM duty raises the allowed current. The PWP thermal pad lets it carry more current or run cooler than PW.

Outputs can be paralleled for more current. For the PW package the allowed current of one, two, four or eight paralleled channels stays flat up to a duty cycle near 35 % and falls as the duty rises toward 100 %.

A write shifts 8 bits per device into DIN, MSB first (D8 first), on CLK rising edges, then a LATCH rising edge transfers them into the data register. With devices chained, bits for the last device in the chain go first: 16 clocks load two devices, the first byte passing through device 1 to device 2. Data leaves on DOUT after CLK falling edges.
A short low pulse on LATCH copies the 16-bit fault register to the shift register; 16 clocks then shift it out on DOUT, F16 first. In a chain each further device adds 16 clocks.

Five commands are coded as four consecutive LATCH-low intervals, split by short LATCH-high pulses, each holding a set number of CLK pulses: 1-2-2-3 writes the control register, 1-4-2-3 reads it back, 1-4-4-3 reads back the data register, 1-2-4-3 clears the fault register and 1-6-6-3 is PWM Start. After Write Control Register, the next 8 bits per device (C8 first) go to the control register. After Read Control Register or Read Data Register, that register is copied to the shift register and clocked out on DOUT, letting the host check what was programmed. The fault reset command clears all fault bits of all chained devices together. PWM Start sends active outputs straight into PWM, skipping the rest of the energizing time.

An output runs in two phases: energizing at 100 % duty for the time in C4:C1 (0 to 300 ms), then PWM chopping at the duty in C7:C5 (12.5 % to 87.5 % in 12.5 % steps, or 0 % for off). Five cases: C8 = 0 (default) keeps outputs fully on; C8 = 1 with C4:C1 = 0000 starts directly in PWM; C8 = 1 with a time and a non-zero duty energizes then chops; C8 = 1 with a time and duty 000 energizes then turns off; C8 = 0 with a time and a duty energizes until a PWM Start command arrives before the timer ends, then chops; if the timer ends first the output stays fully on and later PWM Start commands are ignored. During PWM the average load current is about DC × VM / RL.

An output whose current passes the OCP level (620 mA typ) for the deglitch time is switched off, nFAULT goes low and the channel's OCP bit is set. Writing 0 to that output's data bit, or a Fault Register Reset, clears it; nFAULT releases when no fault bits remain.

While an output is off, a sink of about 30 µA pulls it down; if the pin reads below 1.2 V, an open load is reported, nFAULT goes low and the channel's OL bit (F8:F1) is set. Turning that output on, or a Fault Register Reset, clears it; nFAULT releases when no fault bits remain.
Above the shutdown temperature all outputs turn off and nFAULT goes low. They restart by themselves once the die has cooled, and nFAULT then releases.
If VM drops below the UVLO threshold the whole device stops and its logic resets; it runs again once VM rises back above the threshold. nFAULT is not driven in this state.
All digital inputs pass through an internal noise filter, so noise on a chained serial bus does not upset the outputs while normal serial speeds still pass.
Power-up order does not matter; logic inputs may be present before VM. Once VM is up the device acts on the state of its control pins.

A 0.1 µF ceramic rated for VM goes as close to the VM pin as possible, plus bulk capacitance sized to the application. The bulk value depends on the supply type, allowed ripple, wiring inductance to the supply, the load type and the load's start-up current; supply wiring inductance limits how fast current can be drawn, so too little bulk lets VM sag or rise as the load draws or returns current.

Bypass VM to GND with a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic placed right at the VM pin, joined to the GND pin by a wide trace or ground plane. Put the bulk capacitor near the device too. The nFAULT pull-up goes to a supply within the recommended range of the open-drain outputs.

Shutdown near 150 °C points to too much dissipation, too little heat sinking or too hot an ambient. The PWP thermal pad is soldered to PCB copper; on a multilayer board vias join it to an inner ground plane, and on a board without planes copper is added on either side, joined by thermal vias when on the far side. More copper area lets the part dissipate more.
